display_title: Trustworthy biomedical AI: data design, an evidence ladder and the deployment lifecycle
summary: This methodological review connects biomedical data provenance and endpoint design with model choice, interpretation, causal reasoning, validation and deployment. Its practical contributions are a disease-agnostic roadmap, a six-level evidence ladder and a proposed model-and-data card for reusable research and clinical translation.
research_question: How can biomedical AI studies connect heterogeneous data, appropriate models and interpretable findings to progressively stronger biological evidence and reliable real-world use?
author_summary: The review organizes biomedical AI across multi-omics, imaging and pathology, EHR and text, and longitudinal data. It links each modality’s data-generating process and endpoint choices to validity threats and model selection, covering classical and survival models, deep learning, self-supervised/foundation models, graph-guided learning, multimodal fusion and generative AI. Its evidence ladder distinguishes association, robustness, biological coherence, causal support, perturbation evidence and clinical utility. The evaluation sections connect leakage control, external and temporal validation, calibration, threshold-dependent decisions, uncertainty and subgroup behavior. The translation sections propose a model-and-data card and connect deployment with monitoring, drift detection, accountable updating and auditability. These are methodological proposals and synthesis, with no new data generated or analyzed.

key_findings.context: From prediction to mechanism: interpretability and causal reasoning.

evidence.label: Explanation roles
evidence.value: Global explanations describe population-level reliance; local explanations help investigate individual predictions, atypical cases and extrapolation

evidence.label: Biological anchoring
evidence.value: Pathways, gene programs, cell states and orthogonal assays can strengthen omics interpretation; tissue/spatial assays can anchor imaging or pathology signals

evidence.label: Clinical data context
evidence.value: Orders, codes and notes may describe the care process; temporality and biological anchoring matter when interpreting them mechanistically

evidence.label: Causal framing
evidence.value: Separate prediction from intervention questions; treatment-effect designs require explicit assumptions and aligned eligibility, assignment, covariates and follow-up time zero

key_findings.claim: A six-level evidence ladder gives researchers a language for positioning AI-derived findings.
key_findings.context: A proposed hierarchy connecting associative findings with stronger mechanistic and translational support.

evidence.label: Stages
evidence.value: Association; robustness; biological coherence; causal support; perturbation evidence; clinical utility

evidence.label: Progression
evidence.value: Resampling/pipeline/cohort stability, orthogonal biological agreement, assumption-aware causal analysis, and experimental perturbation add different kinds of support

evidence.label: Top level
evidence.value: Clinical utility requires actionable, calibrated decisions and benefit in realistic evaluation, ideally including prospective assessment

evidence.label: Use of the ladder
evidence.value: Lower-rung findings remain useful when their claims match the evidence; the ladder is not a requirement that every study reach clinical utility

key_findings.claim: Evaluation is linked to transportability, probability quality and the consequences of decisions.

evidence.label: Evaluation boundaries
evidence.value: Prevent preprocessing contamination, nonindependent samples across splits and downstream-care proxies; separate model selection from evaluation

evidence.label: Transportability
evidence.value: Cross-institution, cross-platform and temporal validation probe different shifts

evidence.label: Beyond ranking
evidence.value: Calibration, clinically meaningful horizons, decision curves/net benefit and context-specific thresholds complement discrimination

evidence.label: Reliability
evidence.value: Assess missingness, perturbations, uncertainty under shift and explicit failure modes, with subgroup performance treated as part of scientific validity

key_findings.source_locator: Validation, generalization, and reliability, manuscript lines 519-602, physical PDF pp. 27-31.

key_findings.claim: The proposed model-and-data card connects reproducible reporting with a maintained deployment lifecycle.

evidence.label: Card content
evidence.value: Data provenance/inclusion criteria; endpoint time anchoring; leakage-safe splits and preprocessing; intended population/horizon; validation; uncertainty; calibration; thresholds; subgroup performance

evidence.label: Workflow integration
evidence.value: Specify who uses the output, at what point in care, what information is available and what action it supports

evidence.label: Lifecycle
evidence.value: Monitor performance and drift; track model/data versions; document audit trails and use accountable recalibration/updating

qa.question: What is the main contribution and research genre?
qa.answer: It is a disease-agnostic methodological review and proposed conceptual framework. It connects data and endpoints to models, interpretation, causal reasoning, evaluation and deployment. The specific proposals include a six-level evidence ladder and a model-and-data card. The article reports no new data generation or analysis.

qa.question: How does the framework help with heterogeneous biomedical data and endpoints?
qa.answer: It asks researchers to identify how each modality was generated and what the endpoint represents. Omics batch effects, imaging/site signatures, clinical care-process proxies and longitudinal timing create different validity threats. Operational prediction targets, mechanistic phenotypes, index times and prediction windows should be aligned with the question and intended use.

qa.question: How are model families and multimodal choices compared?
qa.answer: The review covers classical/survival models, deep learning, self-supervised/foundation models, graph/knowledge-guided AI, multimodal fusion and generative AI. It relates each to its data and evaluation needs. Early, intermediate and late fusion differ in how they handle scales, missing modalities and cross-modal interactions; larger representations or attention weights do not supply validation on their own.

qa.question: What distinguishes explanation from stronger mechanistic or causal support?
qa.answer: The review distinguishes population-level global explanations from case-level local explanations and recommends checking stability, biological coherence and orthogonal measurements. Pathway or cell-state summaries and spatial/tissue assays can help anchor model signals. Intervention questions require causal assumptions and aligned time zero, rather than interpreting feature importance as an intervention effect.

qa.question: What are the six levels of the evidence ladder?
qa.answer: They are association, robustness, biological coherence, causal support, perturbation evidence and clinical utility. Each adds a different type of support: stability across reasonable analyses or cohorts; agreement with biological systems; assumption-aware intervention reasoning; experimental manipulation; and actionable decisions with benefit in realistic evaluation. The authors explicitly retain the value of studies at lower rungs when claims match their support.

qa.question: What should evaluation add beyond a single discrimination metric?
qa.answer: The review connects leakage-safe splitting and preprocessing to external, cross-platform and temporal tests. Calibration, prediction horizons and decision-dependent thresholds complement ranking metrics. Missingness, perturbations, uncertainty under shift and subgroup performance help characterize where a model is reliable and how its outputs would affect decisions.

qa.question: What does the proposed model-and-data card document?
qa.answer: It brings together provenance and inclusion criteria, time-anchored endpoints, splitting and preprocessing, intended population and horizon, validation, uncertainty, calibration, thresholds and subgroup performance. The review connects this documentation with workflow integration, version tracking, monitoring, drift detection, audit trails and accountable updating.

qa.question: When is this paper useful to cite, and which source version was read?
qa.answer: It provides a methodological rationale for data and endpoint design, an evidence-strength discussion, and guidance for evaluation, reporting and deployment. The Cardiff repository Journal Pre-proof under the same formal DOI supplies the complete main text and five conceptual figure captions used for this summary.

limitations: This is a narrative methodological synthesis and proposed framework, without a reported systematic-search/selection protocol or quantitative pooling; 124 references are a bibliography count.
The evidence ladder, model-and-data card and lifecycle guidance are proposals rather than newly tested clinical instruments; the article reports no new data generated or analyzed.

The read source is the repository Journal Pre-proof, whose publisher notice says it is not the definitive Version of Record. Five conceptual diagrams are summarized from the accompanying body and captions; no diagram-image audit is claimed.
